report:
The evidence does not support the "no" hypothesis — current evidence leans toward a modest but real benefit, though results are mixed and dose-dependent.

**Summary of evidence:**

Early large trials were discouraging. A rigorous double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of cranberry juice in 319 college-aged women found no reduction in recurrent UTI risk compared to placebo (academic.oup.com/cid/article-abstract/52/1/23/406427). Similarly, a noninferiority trial comparing cranberry capsules to low-dose antibiotics in 221 premenopausal women found cranberry less effective than antibiotics for prevention (jamanetwork.com/journals/jamainternalmedicine/fullarticle/1105854).

However, the updated 2023 Cochrane systematic review — considered the highest-quality synthesis, pooling 50 RCTs and ~8,857 participants — found cranberry products reduced symptomatic, culture-confirmed UTI risk by roughly 26% overall, with the clearest benefit specifically in women with recurrent UTIs, as well as in children and other high-risk groups (cobfoundation.org/health-information/cranberry-vs-d-mannose-for-uti-prevention/; researchgate.net/publication/269400737_Cranberries_for_preventing_urinary_tract_infections_Review).

More targeted RCTs using standardized, high-dose proanthocyanidin (PAC) extracts (≥36 mg/day) — rather than dilute juice — have shown more consistent benefit, and a 2024 meta-analysis focused specifically on high-PAC cranberry products in women with recurrent UTI found a protective effect (link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12894-021-00811-w; frontiersin.org/journals/nutrition/articles/10.3389/fnut.2024.1422121/full).

**Conclusion:** The claim that cranberry juice/extract does *not* help is an oversimplification. Older, lower-quality juice-based trials showed no benefit, explaining the "no" answer's origin. But the best current evidence (2023 Cochrane review, high-PAC dose trials) shows a real, moderate reduction in recurrent UTI risk in women — juice alone is weaker/less reliable than standardized high-dose extracts.
